name: og-31-protometabolism-to-amphiphiles
gate_reason: Partial Gate C (self-compartmentation), QUALIFIED. Under a REDUCED-coupling membrane model (retention reduces effective washout; finite access reduces effective feed crossing — explicitly NOT the MD-resolved permeability PMF, which is study 32 / viva-md-membrane = full Gate C), an endogenous membrane pays for itself on PERSISTENCE but not throughput. On the Gate-B pore-concentrated, sustained A1 carbon-fixing network (NOT autocatalytic — A2 refuted), at Jordan-2019 vent-calibrated retention 0.905 / access 0.997 (grounded, not tuned), the membrane raises the standing metabolite pool to ~2.9× the no-membrane ablation (pays on persistence) while net fixation flux is ~0.6× (lower — throughput is feed-limited, so reduced washout grows the pool, not the rate; this is the physically-expected result, not a shortfall: compartmentalization buys retention/concentration, not faster chemistry). Windowed: the persistence benefit holds for access ≳ 0.45 and inverts below (a too-tight membrane starves the feed; the vent-calibrated point sits inside). Four qualifications: persistence-only, windowed, reduced coupling, and PARTIAL (full Gate C = study 32 + the real MD coupling). og-31's Martini-MD cohesion is the complementary "makes a membrane" half.
title: Protometabolism to Amphiphiles
claim: Under a reduced-coupling membrane model - retention reduces effective washout, finite access reduces effective feed crossing, explicitly NOT the MD-resolved permeability PMF (that is study 32's full Gate C test) - an endogenous membrane pays for itself on persistence but not on throughput. On the Gate-B pore-concentrated network, which is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing metabolism and NOT autocatalytic (A2 is refuted under vent conditions), a membrane at the Jordan-2019 vent-calibrated setting (retention 0.905, access 0.997; grounded, not tuned) raises the standing metabolite pool to about 2.9x the no-membrane ablation, while net carbon-fixation flux is about 0.6x - lower, because throughput is feed-limited, so reduced washout grows the pool rather than the rate. The benefit is windowed: it holds for membrane access down to about 0.45 and inverts below that (a too-tight membrane starves the feed and the retained pool falls below the open system), with the vent-calibrated access inside the window. This is the "benefits from it" half of Gate C, complementing og-31's Martini-MD cohesion (the "makes a membrane" half); the structurally-resolved coupling is study 32.
question: Can actual metabolic products — not supplied amphiphiles — yield membrane-forming amphiphile mixtures under vent-local conditions?
hypothesis: Carbon-chain extension, headgroup generation and competing hydrolysis acting on the real product pool from study 30 will produce a chain-length and headgroup distribution whose concentration reaches the measured critical aggregation concentration and a stable phase window; if losses (hydrolysis, dilution) keep concentrations below that window, no assembly is claimed.
experiment: Transform the study-30 precursor pool via modeled chain-extension/headgroup/hydrolysis chemistry, track chain-length and headgroup distributions, concentrations and losses, and test against measured critical aggregation and phase-stability data — with zero exogenous amphiphile input.
proposed_mechanisms: carbon-chain extension from real metabolic precursors
headgroup generation and competing hydrolysis / degradation losses
concentration vs the measured critical aggregation concentration (CAC) and phase window
proposed_models_methods: RDKit chain-extension / headgroup generation + precursor enumeration   [to-build: viva_reaction_atlas]
OpenMM/LAMMPS composition-dependent assembly + permeability closure     [to-build: viva_md_membrane]
PubChem / ORD amphiphile species identities and properties
measured CAC / phase-stability benchmarks for independent validation (evidence standard

model_approach.prose: Study 31 is where chemistry meets compartment, and the hard rule is evidence standard #2: no untracked amphiphile feed. Every amphiphile must come from the study-30 product pool through explicit modeled chemistry, with hydrolysis and dilution as real sinks. The assembly claim is tested against measured critical aggregation concentrations and phase windows, not a chosen threshold — if the modeled pool never reaches the experimental window, the study reports that the vent-local chemistry is insufficient on its own, and names what is missing.

behavior_tests.name: membrane-benefit-persistence
behavior_tests.description: On the Gate-B pore-concentrated network, an endogenous membrane (reduced retention/access coupling, Jordan-2019 vent-calibrated) raises the standing metabolite pool (total organic carbon) above a matched no-endogenous-membrane ablation at equal external feed — the membrane pays for itself on persistence (the Gate C benefit criterion, retention branch).

pass_if.detail: membrane TOC exceeds the ablation TOC (else no persistence benefit)

behavior_tests.name: membrane-benefit-access-window
behavior_tests.description: The persistence benefit is located as a window in membrane access — it holds for access down to ~0.45 and inverts below (a too-tight membrane starves the feed; the retained pool drops below the open system). The vent-calibrated access sits inside the window.

measure.detail: membrane TOC vs ablation across an access sweep; locate the inversion boundary

pass_if.detail: a bounded access window where membrane TOC exceeds ablation, with a located failure boundary

behavior_tests.name: membrane-benefit-throughput
behavior_tests.description: Net carbon-fixation flux (throughput) under the membrane vs the ablation — expected to be flat/lower (feed-limited), not improved. Reported to make the persistence-vs-throughput split explicit.

pass_if.detail: reported either way (the physically-expected null is not a gate failure)

decision_test: The model must reach an experimentally measured assembly window (critical aggregation + phase stability) using ONLY amphiphiles produced from real metabolic products — no exogenous amphiphile feed (evidence standard #2). Falling short of the measured window is an accepted negative result that names the missing chemistry, reported not tuned (evidence standard #6, #8).

findings.statement: Under the reduced-coupling model, at the Jordan-2019 vent-calibrated retention 0.905 / access 0.997, an endogenous membrane raises the standing metabolite pool (TOC) to about 2.9x the no-membrane ablation on the Gate-B pore-concentrated carbon-fixing network - the membrane pays for itself on persistence. Guardrail: this network is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing metabolism, not autocatalytic (A2 is refuted), so this is "a persisting network makes a membrane that pays for itself," not autocatalysis.

Net carbon-fixation flux under the membrane is about 0.6x the ablation - lower, not higher. Throughput is feed-limited, so reduced washout grows the standing pool, not the fixation rate; the benefit is on persistence, not throughput, and is reported as such. (The physically-expected result, not a shortfall: compartmentalization buys retention/concentration, not faster chemistry.)

The persistence benefit is windowed - it holds for membrane access down to about 0.45 and inverts below ~0.45, where a too-tight membrane starves the feed and the retained pool drops below the open system. The failure boundary is located and the vent-calibrated access (0.997) sits inside the window (mirrors Gate B's windowed discipline).

This is a reduced-coupling membrane model (retention/access), explicitly NOT the MD-resolved permeability PMF. It is the "benefits from it" half of Gate C and complements og-31's Martini-MD cohesion (the "makes a membrane" half). The structurally-resolved coupling (amphiphile composition to permeability to retention) and thus full Gate C requires study 32 (First Self-Maintaining Protocell) plus the viva-md-membrane coupling (to-build).

As in Gate B, the network_connected proxy is brittle at high standing pool - membrane connectivity reads 0 at high TOC accumulation. This is flagged and does not change the persistence result, which is based on the standing metabolite pool (TOC), not connectivity.

membrane-benefit-persistence.detail: At Jordan-2019 vent-calibrated retention 0.905 / access 0.997, the membrane raises the standing metabolite pool (TOC) to 2.93x the no-membrane ablation on the Gate-B pore-concentrated network (equal external feed) - the membrane pays for itself on persistence.

membrane-benefit-access-window.detail: The persistence benefit is windowed: membrane TOC exceeds the ablation for access >= ~0.45 and inverts below (0.45 -> 1.02x, 0.40 -> 0.86x), a located failure boundary where a too-tight membrane starves the feed. The vent-calibrated access 0.997 sits inside the window.

limitations: The membrane benefit here is measured under a REDUCED-COUPLING model (retention reduces effective washout; finite access reduces effective feed crossing), not the MD-resolved permeability PMF - it is the "benefits from it" half of Gate C only. The full, structurally-resolved coupling (amphiphile composition to permeability to metabolite retention), and whether the compartment is genuinely self-maintaining, requires study 32 plus viva-md-membrane (to-build). The benefit is persistence-only (standing pool ~2.9x) and feed-limited on throughput (flux ~0.6x), and windowed in membrane access (inverts below ~0.45; vent-calibrated point inside). network_connected is brittle at high TOC (cross-ref Gate B) and is not the basis of the persistence result.
